subject: Capacity check and provisional node request for Clarion PoC
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@clarionlabs.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example, ben_carter@redwood.example
Date: 2028-05-14T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity check + provisional node request for Clarion PoC

Hi Vanessa / Ben,

Quick ask — we have a PoC kickoff with Clarion Labs next month and want to verify that Redwood can provision the right GPU footprint for the trial window (target start: 2028-06-01). High-level requirements attached (clarion_poc_requirements.xlsx). Key asks:

- Preferred region: us-west (low-latency to their infra)
- Model family: proprietary LLaMA-derivative, ~175B; Clarion will accept int8/4-bit quantized runs if verified
- Sustained throughput: 120 tokens/sec aggregate across 6 concurrency lanes (peak 12 concurrent sessions)
- Estimated monthly hours: ~1,200 GPU-hours during PoC ramp
- Preferred hardware: A100 80GB (if not available, they will accept A100-40GB or Ampere equivalents)

Could Redwood operations run a quick availability check and advise whether a soft hold / provisional earmark is possible for ~30 days while clarion finalizes SOW? If a soft-hold is doable, what is the scope (number of nodes, earliest activation, and any cooling/thermal constraints we should flag)?

Thanks — happy to hop on 20-min call if that helps.

Cheers,
Samantha Lee
Director, ML Engineering
Clarion Labs

Attachments: clarion_poc_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example>

Samantha — thanks for the clear requirements and the attachment. Looping in Ben (sales ops) and Rishi (capacity planning) to validate fleet fit and to open a provisional hold if feasible. Grace from CS will help with onboarding constraints if we proceed.

Preliminary notes from me:
- We can run a quick inventory map for us-west AZ and return a recommended node allocation (prefer: A100-80GB).
- We can offer a soft, non-billable hold for up to 21 days by opening an internal reservation ticket; if Clarion needs 30 days we can escalate to a sales credit hold, but that requires deal approval.
- Please confirm the exact deal_id (if you have one) and whether the PoC requires isolated dedicated pool or shared but pin-zoned instances.

I'll ask Rishi to give an ops-level readout and propose an alternative config that trades quantization for fewer GPUs if needed. Ben — can you open the soft-hold and include the tentative dates?

Best,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example>

Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.example, Samantha Lee <samantha@clarionlabs.com>
Date: 2028-05-15T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity check + provisional node request for Clarion PoC

Vanessa / Ben / Samantha — I ran a quick fit assessment against the us-west AZ pool. Summary below (ops-level):

- Current usable A100-80GB inventory in us-west AZ: ~14 units (after normal buffer).
- Requested footprint estimate for Clarion PoC (baseline):
  - Target performance (120 tokens/sec, 12 concurrency peak) translates to ~3 A100-80GB instances if model runs at int8 with batching and KV cache reuse.
  - If Clarion insists on fp16, plan is ~6 A100-80GB instances to sustain latency SLOs.
- Thermal/affinity notes: our us-west racks are near peak thermal at sustained multi-GPU runs; long-duration PoC runs may need node spreading across 2 AZ pods to avoid thermal throttling. That increases network egress complexity slightly but is doable.

Options to reduce required GPUs (trade-offs):
- Recommend validating int4 quantization (or 4-bit LLM QAT) — our benchmark shows a 30–40% reduction in GPU-hours for this model family with acceptable accuracy loss for PoC.
- Use a sequence-length-aware batching policy (we can set per-lane max_seq_length=512) and enable prefix caching for repeated contexts — typical for Clarion's use-case and could cut token compute by ~20%.

If you want a provisional reservation, ops can earmark 4 A100-80GB nodes across two racks for a 21-day soft-hold (start 2028-05-18). That leaves a small operational buffer for other deals while keeping the PoC viable. If Clarion confirms fp16-only and wants an isolated pool, we'll require a formal reserved capacity (contract addendum) because that reduces our pooling flexibility.

I'll create JIRA-OPS-12987 with the proposed spread and include a quick perf simulation (link below). If you want me to run a sample int4 perf run against the Clarion model artifacts, we can schedule an ops test next week — we'd need the model artefacts and a simple evaluation prompt set.

— Rishi
Head of Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference

We will upload a minimal eval prompt set and a model snapshot to the drive link Rishi provided by EOD 2028-05-17. Can you confirm the ops ticket number and soft-hold terms once the reservation is created?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Samantha
